paper_metadata.title: In-situ synthesizing Al–Y precipitates in Mg–3Y/Al composites for enhancing high-temperature tensile properties
paper_metadata.journal: Journal of Materials Research and Technology

evidence.quote: The Mg–3Y/Al composites were prepared using a customized Mg–3Y alloy ingot and pure Al foils of 30 μm, 15 μm, and 10 μm thicknesses.
Mg–3Y/Al composites were produced through accumulated rolling bonding.
To evaluate the thermal stability of the Al2Y precipitates and Mg – 3Y/ Al composites, the AR3 composites were further heat-treated at 400 ◦C for 0 – 4 h.
the tensile strength of the Mg–3Y/Al composite exhibits increased strength (~273.9 MPa) but reduced ductility (~3.5%) compared to the base Mg–3Y alloy (~191.0 MPa, ~30%)

evidence.quote: This assembly was preheated at 400 °C for 20 min in an argon-filled muffle furnace, followed by hot rolling bonding. After three passes of rolling, resulting in an accumulated reduction of 50%, the Mg–3Y/Al composites were obtained.
Subsequently, diffusion annealing was conducted at 400 °C for 6 h to facilitate element diffusion and reaction in the as-rolled Mg–3Y/Al composites.
Through 1 to 3 repeated operations, labeled as AR1, AR2, and AR3 respectively, composites with varying layer thicknesses and precipitate contents were achieved.

attributes.location: interface layer adjacent to PFR layer (Region 3)

evidence.quote: many second phases with a chain shape exist in the interface layer adjacent to the PFR layer. The enlarged view of Region 3 shows that the chain phases consist of many continuously distributed short rod-like precipitates.
According to the PDF cards, these diffraction peaks, mainly match the standard diffraction peaks of α-Mg and Al2Y
a minor quantity of the Mg-RE phase with a size of ~2 μm is also present

Al2Y precipitates ranging in size from 40 to 300 nm were synthesized within the Mg – 3Y/Al composites. In the AR3 sample, the volume fraction of the interface layer containing these Al2Y precipitates can reach as high as 74%.
the Al2Y particle size in the interface layer is consistently within the range of 40 nm – 300 nm, with an average size of approximately 100 nm, even after further annealing at 400 ◦C for 0 – 4 h
the extruded Mg–3Y alloy exhibits a complete equiaxed grain with an average grain size of approximately 15.7 μm
In the AR3 sample, the interface layer was thicker than the region within the Mg–3Y layer lacking precipitates, with the volume fraction of the interface layer reaching approximately 74%.
The Al2Y particles in the interface layer act as nucleation sites for recrystallization, promoting the formation of fine recrystallized grains.

the IPF color maps revealed that grains within the interface layer appeared red, while the pole figure (PF) indicated a pronounced texture alignment, with the c-axis of most grains approaching the ND direction.

The microstructure analysis suggests that the high strength and low ductility of Mg–3Y/Al composites may stem from factors such as fine grain size, residual dislocations from the ARB process, and Al2Y precipitates
